chunks: They will do you no harm but annoyance; and if they fight you they will only turn their backs, then no help will reach them.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the enemy's ability to harm believers in battle?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Battle of Uhud, highlighting the psychological fragility of the disbelievers when divine support is withdrawn. It underscores the principle that victory is contingent upon Allah's aid rather than numerical strength, offering reassurance to the faithful amidst trials. The mention of 'not being granted victory' (la yunsarun) serves as a definitive promise of their ultimate defeat in both worldly and spiritual realms.
